note: Rewritten from entry 93 in Roonwal & Chhotani (1997), the original in English. The original is itself an account based on the examination of all the type specimens of the species; the authors pointed out that the original description (Chatterjee & Thakur 1964) recorded the alate as dark chestnut brown with dark smoky grey wings, and after examining all the type specimens changed this to a brown body with colourless transparent wings, which is the account followed here. The diagnostic characters follow the keys to the alates and soldiers in that work (p. 571–572). The synonymy list, literature citations, figure numbers, distribution and biological notes have been omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is a large species within the genus (body length 10.00–13.50 mm), head length to mandibular base 3.20–3.70, width 2.30–2.60 mm, the head rectangular to oval, sides slightly convex and converging forwards, antennal sockets prominent and deep, fontanelle oval, mandibles relatively short (mandible length to head length ratio about 0.60–0.67); the similarly large congener chakratensis has a nearly rectangular head with nearly parallel sides, inconspicuous and shallow antennal sockets, a nearly circular fontanelle and relatively longer mandibles (that ratio 0.73–0.76). The alate has a pale yellowish brown head capsule and 20–22-segmented antennae, the occipital suture visible but its lateral arms indistinct, and rather short wing scales (forewing scale length 1.0–1.13, hindwing 0.75–0.85 mm); in bengalensis the occipital suture is visible only in its posterior part and the wing scales are longer (forewing 1.3–1.5, hindwing 0.73–0.85 mm).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and body brown; antennae, legs and lower part of the thorax yellowish brown; postclypeus and labrum yellowish brown; wings transparent, almost colourless. Head, body and legs densely hairy. Body length with wings 15.80–16.40 mm, without wings 8.60–9.10 mm. Head capsule nearly circular, slightly wider than long (width including eyes 1.65–1.80, length to mandibular base 1.40–1.55 mm); Y-suture present, its lateral arms not very distinct. Fontanelle minute, situated in the middle of the head. Antennae 20–22-segmented; segment 2 variable, nearly equal to or longer than segment 3, or equal to segments 3 and 4 together; length increasing slightly from segment 5 onwards. Eyes large, nearly black, nearly circular (long diameter 0.40–0.45 mm), 0.08 mm from the antennal sockets. Ocelli colourless and transparent, white (long diameter 0.18–0.20 mm); the minimum distance between the eye and the ocellus 0.08 mm, less than half the long diameter of the ocellus. Postclypeus orange-yellow, without a median line, trapezoidal, swollen, with a few setiform hairs; length less than half its width, anterior margin slightly concave. Anteclypeus white, hairless, nearly as long as the postclypeus. Mandibles as in the generic diagnosis. Pronotum flat, much wider than long (length 0.80–0.85, width 1.40–1.48 mm), narrower than the head width including eyes; anterior margin concave with a weak median notch; posterior margin rounded with a weak median emargination. Femora long and swollen; tibiae long and slender; tibial spur formula 3:2:2; tarsi 3-segmented. Wing reticulation distinct. Forewing longer than hindwing, length 13.00–13.70 mm; hindwing scale length 11.75–12.40 mm. Venation as in the generic diagnosis; cubitus of the forewing with 21–23 branches, of the hindwing with 19–23. Abdomen elongate, hairy; cerci 2-segmented; abdominal styli absent.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and postclypeus reddish brown; base of the mandibles dark brown, the rest nearly black; anteclypeus white; antennae and labrum pale brown; pronotum yellowish brown; legs and abdomen yellow. Head and body rather densely hairy. Body length 10.00–13.50 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular, much longer than wide (length to mandibular base 3.20–3.70, width 2.30–2.60 mm); sides slightly converging forwards; posterior margin rounded. Fontanelle oval, small, situated slightly in front of the middle of the head. Antennae 16–19-segmented; segment 2 shortest, segment 3 longer, segments 4 and 5 subequal, length increasing from segment 6 onwards. Eyes small, reduced, close to the antennal sockets. Ocelli absent. Postclypeus broad, its boundary with the frons indistinct, length about half its width; anterior margin convex, sparsely hairy; anteclypeus white, narrow, hairless. Labrum rounded, dome-shaped; length 0.35–0.48, width 0.55–0.63 mm; anterior margin and surface with a few hairs. Mandibles long (2.00–2.30 mm), stout, sabre-shaped, incurved at the tip; inner margin smooth apart from a few fine serrations. Left mandible with one fine serration below the middle; right mandible with a small serration on the upper part of the basal 1/3 and, at the base, another larger tooth-like process. Postmentum long, club-shaped, 2.45–2.70 mm long; the club divided into an anterior lobe and a wider posterior lobe (maximum width 0.85–1.00 mm), narrowing backwards to the waist (minimum width 0.30–0.40 mm, situated slightly above the middle) and then widening again towards the base. Pronotum hairy, flat, trapezoidal; much wider than long (width 1.75–2.10, length 1.15–1.35 mm); anterior margin with a deep median notch; sides curved towards the posterior margin, the posterior margin with a median emargination. Femora thick and swollen; tibiae long and slender; tibial spur formula 3:2:2; tarsi 3-segmented. Abdomen elongate; cerci 2-segmented; abdominal styli absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule and postclypeus yellow, frons paler; labrum yellow to yellowish brown; antennae and legs paler than the head; body milky white. Head rather hairy, body densely hairy. Body length 7.50–9.00 mm. Head capsule nearly circular, widest in its anterior part (length to mandibular base 1.55–1.85, width 1.70–2.00 mm), posterior part rounded; Y-suture indistinct. Eyes and ocelli not visible. Antennae 17–20-segmented, segment 4 shortest. Postclypeus broad, slightly swollen, with a few hairs; anterior margin concave, posterior margin convex. Anteclypeus white, hairless, trapezoidal. Labrum and mandibles as in the alate. Pronotum flat, wider than long (width 1.40–1.65, length 0.63–0.95 mm); anterior margin slightly turned up and concave; posterior margin convex with a median emargination. Legs and abdomen as in the soldier.
